editorial:
A loving father fights to save his teenage son from meth addiction in this emotional family drama. Steve Carell plays David Sheff, a journalist who tries everything to help Nic, played by Timothée Chalamet. The movie jumps between happy childhood memories and the dark reality of Nic's drug use, showing how addiction doesn't just hurt the user but tears apart the whole family. You feel the desperation in every scene as David searches for answers that may not exist. It's heavy and emotional, but it never feels fake or preachy. The bond between father and son stays at the center, making every relapse hit harder.

Chalamet gives a raw, believable performance that makes Nic's struggle feel real, while Carell shows a father's helpless love perfectly. The pacing is slow and deliberate, which works for the story but may test your patience if you want fast action. The film doesn't offer easy solutions, which is honest but also draining. If you enjoy emotional family dramas, this is a must-see. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Nic relapses again and disappears, leaving David heartbroken and forced to accept he cannot control his son's addiction. After a long silence, Nic finally reaches out and agrees to get help. The movie ends with Nic clean and writing his own story, while David cautiously hopes this time will last. There is no miracle cure shown, just a fragile new beginning built on honesty and hard work.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional family dramas and true stories.
